name: Testing Layer
description: Describes how the system is verified: test strategies and plans, suites and cases, fixtures and test data, mocks and stubs, coverage targets and summaries, and the environments tests run in (IEEE 829-2008 test documentation). Test files, fixtures and test configuration are evidence for elements here; the production code under test belongs to the layer it implements. Modelling rules: each testing type has one composing parent. A test coverage model composes its coverage targets, input space partitions, context variations, environment factors, exclusions and coverage summary; a coverage target composes its target input fields, outcome categories, coverage requirements and test case sketches; a coverage requirement composes its input partition selections; a partition composes its values; a test case sketch composes its input selections. A test case sketch validates the one coverage requirement it exercises and references the context variation and outcome category it combines; each input selection references the partition value it picks. A coverage requirement references the context variations and outcome categories it needs, and reaches partition values only through its selections. A target input field references its partition and the field under test (an API parameter, schema property or UX component), so partitions stay reusable across fields; a selection references the values it picks, and a partition dependency references its trigger value and the partition it affects. Summaries report and never validate: a coverage summary aggregates the per-target summaries, a target coverage summary references its target, and both reference the gaps and exclusions they count. Gaps and exclusions reference the requirement or target they concern, and an exclusion references the gap it waives. Context variations reference the environment factors they fix, and environment factors reference only technology nodes and system software. A coverage target covers the production artifact it names; a test case sketch tests what it exercises, requires the software it runs on and accesses the stores holding its fixture data; the model covers only the application component, UX application or API document it is for. Requirements and summaries reach no other layer. The model carries the plan-level motivation links (it supports goals, satisfies principles, constraints and requirements, and measures outcomes), and test case sketches satisfy the requirements they verify.
